questions.question_text: In Euler's formula $v-e+f=2$, which regions are counted by $f$?

options.text: Every region the edges cut the page into, including the unbounded region outside the drawing.
Only the regions completely fenced in by edges.
options.why: Leaves out the outer region, which is the omission that makes Euler's formula appear to give $1$ instead of $2$.

options.text: Every region fenced in by edges, plus one region for each vertex of the drawing.
options.why: Counts vertices as though they were regions, when $v$ already counts them separately in the formula.

options.text: Only the regions bounded by exactly three edges.
options.why: Invents a condition on the shape of a region; a face may be bounded by any number of edges.

questions.solution_text:
A face is a region the edges divide the page into.
The region stretching away outside the whole drawing is one of those regions, so $f$ counts **every** region, the outer one included.

options.why: Counts only the two fenced-in regions and leaves out the outer region, so the formula appears to fail.
Misses the edge $BE$ when counting edges, although the region it creates is still counted in $f$.
Counts an extra vertex where the edge $BE$ meets the ring, although both of its ends are at vertices already counted.

questions.solution_text:
The dots give $v=6$ and the lines give $e=7$.
The edge $BE$ splits the inside of the ring into two regions, and the outer region is a third face, so $f=3$.
$v-e+f$
$=6-7+3$
$=2$

questions.question_text: A connected planar graph has $8$ vertices and $13$ edges. How many faces does it have?

options.why: Computes $e-v$ and forgets to add the $2$ when rearranging $v-e+f=2$.
Gives the number of fenced-in regions, leaving the outer region out of the face count.
Adds the vertices and edges instead of rearranging the formula to $f=2-v+e$.

questions.question_text: A connected planar graph has $11$ vertices and $7$ faces. How many edges does it have?

options.why: Subtracts the face count instead of adding it, computing $11-7+2$ rather than $11+7-2$.
Adds $2$ instead of subtracting it when rearranging $v-e+f=2$ to make $e$ the subject.
Adds the vertices and faces but forgets to subtract the $2$ from Euler's formula.

questions.question_text: A connected planar graph has $13$ edges and $6$ faces. How many vertices does it have?

options.why: Computes $e-f$ and forgets to add the $2$ when rearranging $v-e+f=2$.
Adds the face count instead of subtracting it, computing $2+13+6$ rather than $2+13-6$.
Adds the edges and faces, using $v=e+f$ instead of the rearranged formula.
Leaves the unbounded outer region out of the face count.
Does not count the two inner vertices $F$ and $G$, using $v=5$ in the formula.
Reports the value of $v-e+f$ rather than the value of $f$ it was meant to produce.

questions.question_text: Ben says he has drawn a connected planar graph with $6$ vertices, $8$ edges and $3$ faces. Which response is correct?

options.text: No — the counts give $v-e+f=1$, so no such graph exists.
Yes — the counts satisfy Euler's formula.
options.why: Adds the outer region to Ben's face count as though he had left it out, and $6-8+4$ does give $2$.

options.text: No — the counts give $v-e+f=-5$, so no such graph exists.
options.why: Subtracts the face count instead of adding it, computing $6-8-3$ on the way to the verdict.

options.text: No — a connected planar graph can never have more edges than vertices.
options.why: Invents a rule; plenty of planar graphs have more edges than vertices, and only the formula settles it.

questions.solution_text:
$v-e+f$
$=6-8+3$
$=1$
Euler's formula requires $2$ for every connected planar drawing, so Ben's counts are impossible.

questions.question_text: A connected planar network of paths in a botanic garden has $8$ junctions and fences in $5$ garden beds. How many paths does the network have?

options.why: Uses $f=5$, treating the $5$ beds as the whole face count and forgetting the outer region.
Adds the junction count to the face count but forgets to subtract the $2$ in Euler's formula.
Subtracts the face count instead of adding it, computing $8-6+2$ rather than $8+6-2$.

questions.solution_text:
The $5$ beds are the fenced-in regions, and the outer region is a face as well.
$f=5+1$
$=6$
$v-e+f=2$
$8-e+6=2$
$e=8+6-2$
$=12$

options.why: Counts the pair of edges joining $P$ and $Q$ as a single edge, using $e=4$ in the formula.
Counts the loop as two edges because both of its ends are at $R$, using $e=6$ in the formula.
Uses $f=v+e-2$ instead of $f=2-v+e$, computing $3+5-2$.

questions.solution_text:
The loop is one edge and each of the two edges joining $P$ and $Q$ is counted separately, so $v=3$ and $e=5$.
$v-e+f=2$
$3-5+f=2$
$f=2-3+5$
$=4$
